question.text: Jensen's Alpha = Rp − [Rf + β × (Rm − Rf)]. A portfolio has Rp = 20%, Rm = 12%, Rf = 6%, β = 1.2. Jensen's Alpha is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Required return = 6 + 1.2×(12-6) = 6 + 7.2 = 13.2%. Jensen's Alpha = 20 - 13.2 = 6.8%. The Trap: 7.2% uses wrong math; 8% is raw excess (20-12)—ignoring beta adjustment. Cross-Exam Context: Classic. Manager's Pro-Tip: Positive alpha must persist over 3+ years with statistical significance before attribution to skill, not noise.
